references.text: Describes the daily burnt offering that was to be offered morning and evening, corresponding to the two-part structure of Aaron's sacrifice.
Repeats the regulation concerning the continual offering morning and evening, paralleling the principle of the continuous sacrifice.
Describes the grain offering (mincha) of fine flour, which is the same type of offering mentioned in this verse.
Mentions an ephah as a unit of measurement, relevant to understanding the tenth part of an ephah referred to here.
Describes the anointing of the priest, which forms the background for the expression 'the day he is anointed'.
Relates the anointing of Aaron for priestly service, which provides the context for this particular offering.
Contrasts the daily sacrifices of the Levitical priests with Christ's single sacrifice, showing the fulfillment of the continual offering.
